basic.text: System status, or system help reply
Help message (Information on how to use the receiver or the meaning of a particular non-standard command; this reply is useful only to the human user)
<domain> Service ready
<domain> Service closing transmission channel
Requested mail action okay, completed
User not local; will forward to <forward-path> (See Section 3.4)
Cannot VRFY user, but will accept message and attempt delivery (See Section 3.5.3)
Start mail input; end with <CRLF>.<CRLF>
<domain> Service not available, closing transmission channel (This may be a reply to any command if the service knows it must shut down)
Requested mail action not taken: mailbox unavailable (e.g., mailbox busy or temporarily blocked for policy reasons)
Requested action aborted: local error in processing
Requested action not taken: insufficient system storage
Server unable to accommodate parameters
Syntax error, command unrecognized (This may include errors such as command line too long)
Syntax error in parameters or arguments
Command not implemented (see Section 4.2.4)
Bad sequence of commands
Command parameter not implemented
Requested action not taken: mailbox unavailable (e.g., mailbox not found, no access, or command rejected for policy reasons)
User not local; please try <forward-path> (See Section 3.4)
Requested mail action aborted: exceeded storage allocation
Requested action not taken: mailbox name not allowed (e.g., mailbox syntax incorrect)
Transaction failed (Or, in the case of a connection-opening response, "No SMTP service here")
MAIL FROM/RCPT TO parameters not recognized or not implemented

enhanced.desc: Other undefined status is the only undefined error code. It should be used for all errors for which only the class of the error is known.
enhanced.note: Accepted. Nothing to do.

enhanced.desc: This mailbox address as specified was valid. This status code should be used for positive delivery reports.
enhanced.note: Accepted. Nothing to do.

enhanced.desc: Something was wrong with the protocol necessary to deliver the message to the next hop and the problem cannot be well expressed with any of the other provided detail codes.
enhanced.note: Accepted. Nothing to do.

enhanced.desc: This is a warning sent to the sender when message delivery was successfully but when the delivery required a conversion in which some data was lost. This may also be a permanent error if the sender has indicated that conversion with loss is prohibited for the message.
enhanced.note: Accepted. Nothing to do.

enhanced.sample: UTF-8 string reply is required, but not permitted by the SMTP client
enhanced.desc: This indicates that a reply containing a UTF-8 string is required to show the mailbox name, but that form of response is not permitted by the SMTP client.
enhanced.note: Accepted. Nothing to do.

enhanced.desc: Something related to security caused the message to be returned, and the problem cannot be well expressed with any of the other provided detail codes. This status code may also be used when the condition cannot be further described because of security policies in force.
enhanced.note: Accepted. Nothing to do.

enhanced.desc: Other undefined status is the only undefined error code. It should be used for all errors for which only the class of the error is known.
enhanced.note: Temporary and unspecified. The normal retry schedule handles it.

enhanced.desc: Something about the address specified in the message caused this DSN.
enhanced.note: Temporary problem with the address. Retry, then suppress if it persists.

enhanced.desc: The mailbox specified in the address does not exist. For Internet mail names, this means the address portion to the left of the "@" sign is invalid. This code is only useful for permanent failures.
enhanced.note: Temporary problem with the address. Retry, then suppress if it persists.

enhanced.desc: The destination system specified in the address does not exist or is incapable of accepting mail. For Internet mail names, this means the address portion to the right of the "@" is invalid for mail. This code is only useful for permanent failures.
enhanced.note: Temporary problem with the address. Retry, then suppress if it persists.

enhanced.desc: The destination address was syntactically invalid. This can apply to any field in the address. This code is only useful for permanent failures.
enhanced.note: Temporary problem with the address. Retry, then suppress if it persists.

enhanced.desc: The mailbox address as specified matches one or more recipients on the destination system. This may result if a heuristic address mapping algorithm is used to map the specified address to a local mailbox name.
enhanced.note: Temporary problem with the address. Retry, then suppress if it persists.

enhanced.desc: This mailbox address as specified was valid. This status code should be used for positive delivery reports.
enhanced.note: Temporary problem with the address. Retry, then suppress if it persists.

enhanced.sample: Destination mailbox has moved, No forwarding address
enhanced.desc: The mailbox address provided was at one time valid, but mail is no longer being accepted for that address. This code is only useful for permanent failures.
enhanced.note: Temporary problem with the address. Retry, then suppress if it persists.

enhanced.desc: The sender's address was syntactically invalid. This can apply to any field in the address.
enhanced.note: Temporary problem with the address. Retry, then suppress if it persists.

enhanced.desc: The sender's system specified in the address does not exist or is incapable of accepting return mail. For domain names, this means the address portion to the right of the "@" is invalid for mail.
enhanced.note: Temporary problem with the address. Retry, then suppress if it persists.

enhanced.desc: The mailbox address specified was valid, but the message has been relayed to a system that does not speak this protocol; no further information can be provided.
enhanced.note: Temporary problem with the address. Retry, then suppress if it persists.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when the associated address is marked as invalid using a null MX.
enhanced.note: Temporary problem with the address. Retry, then suppress if it persists.

enhanced.desc: The mailbox exists, but something about the destination mailbox has caused the sending of this DSN.
enhanced.note: The mailbox cannot take it now. Retry with backoff for a few days, then suppress.

enhanced.desc: The mailbox exists, but is not accepting messages. This may be a permanent error if the mailbox will never be re-enabled or a transient error if the mailbox is only temporarily disabled.
enhanced.note: The mailbox cannot take it now. Retry with backoff for a few days, then suppress.

enhanced.desc: The mailbox is full because the user has exceeded a per-mailbox administrative quota or physical capacity. The general semantics implies that the recipient can delete messages to make more space available. This code should be used as a persistent transient failure.
enhanced.note: The mailbox is over quota. It often clears. Retry with backoff for a few days, then suppress.

enhanced.desc: A per-mailbox administrative message length limit has been exceeded. This status code should be used when the per-mailbox message length limit is less than the general system limit. This code should be used as a permanent failure.
enhanced.note: The mailbox cannot take it now. Retry with backoff for a few days, then suppress.

enhanced.desc: The mailbox is a mailing list address and the mailing list was unable to be expanded. This code may represent a permanent failure or a persistent transient failure.
enhanced.note: The mailbox cannot take it now. Retry with backoff for a few days, then suppress.

enhanced.sample: Other or undefined mail system status
enhanced.desc: The destination system exists and normally accepts mail, but something about the system has caused the generation of this DSN.
enhanced.note: The receiving system is short of capacity. Retry, and reduce concurrency if it recurs.

enhanced.desc: Mail system storage has been exceeded. The general semantics imply that the individual recipient may not be able to delete material to make room for additional messages. This is useful only as a persistent transient error.
enhanced.note: The receiving system is short of capacity. Retry, and reduce concurrency if it recurs.

enhanced.desc: The host on which the mailbox is resident is not accepting messages. Examples of such conditions include an imminent shutdown, excessive load, or system maintenance. This is useful for both permanent and persistent transient errors.
enhanced.note: The receiving system is short of capacity. Retry, and reduce concurrency if it recurs.

enhanced.sample: System not capable of selected features
enhanced.desc: Selected features specified for the message are not supported by the destination system. This can occur in gateways when features from one domain cannot be mapped onto the supported feature in another.
enhanced.note: The receiving system is short of capacity. Retry, and reduce concurrency if it recurs.

enhanced.desc: The message is larger than per-message size limit. This limit may either be for physical or administrative reasons. This is useful only as a permanent error.
enhanced.note: The receiving system is short of capacity. Retry, and reduce concurrency if it recurs.

enhanced.desc: The system is not configured in a manner that will permit it to accept this message.
enhanced.note: The receiving system is short of capacity. Retry, and reduce concurrency if it recurs.

enhanced.desc: The message was accepted for relay/delivery, but the requested priority (possibly the implied default) was not honoured. The human readable text after the status code contains the new priority, followed by SP (space) and explanatory human readable text.
enhanced.note: The receiving system is short of capacity. Retry, and reduce concurrency if it recurs.

enhanced.sample: Other or undefined network or routing status
enhanced.desc: Something went wrong with the networking, but it is not clear what the problem is, or the problem cannot be well expressed with any of the other provided detail codes.
enhanced.note: A routing or network problem. Retry, but investigate if it sticks to one destination.

enhanced.desc: The outbound connection attempt was not answered, because either the remote system was busy, or was unable to take a call. This is useful only as a persistent transient error.
enhanced.note: No answer from the destination host. A transport failure, not a mail failure. Investigate if it sticks to one route.

enhanced.desc: The outbound connection was established, but was unable to complete the message transaction, either because of time-out, or inadequate connection quality. This is useful only as a persistent transient error.
enhanced.note: A routing or network problem. Retry, but investigate if it sticks to one destination.

enhanced.desc: The network system was unable to forward the message, because a directory server was unavailable. This is useful only as a persistent transient error. The inability to connect to an Internet DNS server is one example of the directory server failure error.
enhanced.note: A routing or network problem. Retry, but investigate if it sticks to one destination.

enhanced.desc: The mail system was unable to determine the next hop for the message because the necessary routing information was unavailable from the directory server. This is useful for both permanent and persistent transient errors. A DNS lookup returning only an SOA (Start of Administration) record for a domain name is one example of the unable to route error.
enhanced.note: A routing or network problem. Retry, but investigate if it sticks to one destination.

enhanced.desc: The mail system was unable to deliver the message because the mail system was congested. This is useful only as a persistent transient error.
enhanced.note: The receiver is congested. Reduce concurrency for this provider specifically rather than globally.

enhanced.desc: A routing loop caused the message to be forwarded too many times, either because of incorrect routing tables or a user- forwarding loop. This is useful only as a persistent transient error.
enhanced.note: A routing or network problem. Retry, but investigate if it sticks to one destination.

enhanced.desc: The message was considered too old by the rejecting system, either because it remained on that host too long or because the time-to-live value specified by the sender of the message was exceeded. If possible, the code for the actual problem found when delivery was attempted should be returned rather than this code.
enhanced.note: A routing or network problem. Retry, but investigate if it sticks to one destination.

enhanced.desc: Something was wrong with the protocol necessary to deliver the message to the next hop and the problem cannot be well expressed with any of the other provided detail codes.
enhanced.note: A protocol-level hiccup. Retry; if it repeats, the two systems disagree about something.

enhanced.desc: A mail transaction protocol command was issued which was either out of sequence or unsupported. This is useful only as a permanent error.
enhanced.note: A protocol-level hiccup. Retry; if it repeats, the two systems disagree about something.

enhanced.desc: A mail transaction protocol command was issued which could not be interpreted, either because the syntax was wrong or the command is unrecognized. This is useful only as a permanent error.
enhanced.note: A protocol-level hiccup. Retry; if it repeats, the two systems disagree about something.

enhanced.desc: More recipients were specified for the message than could have been delivered by the protocol. This error should normally result in the segmentation of the message into two, the remainder of the recipients to be delivered on a subsequent delivery attempt. It is included in this list in the event that such segmentation is not possible.
enhanced.note: Too many recipients in one transaction. Split the envelope.

enhanced.desc: A valid mail transaction protocol command was issued with invalid arguments, either because the arguments were out of range or represented unrecognized features. This is useful only as a permanent error.
enhanced.note: A protocol-level hiccup. Retry; if it repeats, the two systems disagree about something.

enhanced.desc: A protocol version mis-match existed which could not be automatically resolved by the communicating parties.
enhanced.note: A protocol-level hiccup. Retry; if it repeats, the two systems disagree about something.

enhanced.sample: Authentication Exchange line is too long
enhanced.desc: This enhanced status code SHOULD be returned when the server fails the AUTH command due to the client sending a [BASE64] response which is longer than the maximum buffer size available for the currently selected SASL mechanism. This is useful for both permanent and persistent transient errors.
enhanced.note: A protocol-level hiccup. Retry; if it repeats, the two systems disagree about something.

enhanced.desc: Something about the content of a message caused it to be considered undeliverable and the problem cannot be well expressed with any of the other provided detail codes.
enhanced.note: The receiver could not process the content this time. Retrying rarely helps on its own.

enhanced.desc: The media of the message is not supported by either the delivery protocol or the next system in the forwarding path. This is useful only as a permanent error.
enhanced.note: The receiver could not process the content this time. Retrying rarely helps on its own.

enhanced.desc: The content of the message must be converted before it can be delivered and such conversion is not permitted. Such prohibitions may be the expression of the sender in the message itself or the policy of the sending host.
enhanced.note: The receiver could not process the content this time. Retrying rarely helps on its own.

enhanced.desc: The message content must be converted in order to be forwarded but such conversion is not possible or is not practical by a host in the forwarding path. This condition may result when an ESMTP gateway supports 8bit transport but is not able to downgrade the message to 7 bit as required for the next hop.
enhanced.note: The receiver could not process the content this time. Retrying rarely helps on its own.

enhanced.desc: This is a warning sent to the sender when message delivery was successfully but when the delivery required a conversion in which some data was lost. This may also be a permanent error if the sender has indicated that conversion with loss is prohibited for the message.
enhanced.note: The receiver could not process the content this time. Retrying rarely helps on its own.

enhanced.desc: A conversion was required but was unsuccessful. This may be useful as a permanent or persistent temporary notification.
enhanced.note: The receiver could not process the content this time. Retrying rarely helps on its own.

enhanced.desc: The message content could not be fetched from a remote system. This may be useful as a permanent or persistent temporary notification.
enhanced.note: The receiver could not process the content this time. Retrying rarely helps on its own.

enhanced.sample: Non-ASCII addresses not permitted for that sender/recipient
enhanced.desc: This indicates the reception of a MAIL or RCPT command that non-ASCII addresses are not permitted
enhanced.note: The receiver could not process the content this time. Retrying rarely helps on its own.

enhanced.sample: UTF-8 string reply is required, but not permitted by the SMTP client
enhanced.desc: This indicates that a reply containing a UTF-8 string is required to show the mailbox name, but that form of response is not permitted by the SMTP client.
enhanced.note: The receiver could not process the content this time. Retrying rarely helps on its own.

enhanced.sample: UTF-8 header message cannot be transferred to one or more recipients, so the message must be rejected
enhanced.desc: This indicates that transaction failed after the final "." of the DATA command.
enhanced.note: The receiver could not process the content this time. Retrying rarely helps on its own.

enhanced.desc: This is a duplicate of X.6.8 and is thus deprecated.
enhanced.note: The receiver could not process the content this time. Retrying rarely helps on its own.

enhanced.desc: Something related to security caused the message to be returned, and the problem cannot be well expressed with any of the other provided detail codes. This status code may also be used when the condition cannot be further described because of security policies in force.
enhanced.note: Held for policy reasons, temporarily. This is where most rate limiting lands, so back off before retrying.

enhanced.desc: The sender is not authorized to send to the destination. This can be the result of per-host or per-recipient filtering. This memo does not discuss the merits of any such filtering, but provides a mechanism to report such. This is useful only as a permanent error.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: The sender is not authorized to send a message to the intended mailing list. This is useful only as a permanent error.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.sample: Security conversion required but not possible
enhanced.desc: A conversion from one secure messaging protocol to another was required for delivery and such conversion was not possible. This is useful only as a permanent error.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: A message contained security features such as secure authentication that could not be supported on the delivery protocol. This is useful only as a permanent error.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: A transport system otherwise authorized to validate or decrypt a message in transport was unable to do so because necessary information such as key was not available or such information was invalid.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: A transport system otherwise authorized to validate or decrypt a message was unable to do so because the necessary algorithm was not supported.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: A transport system otherwise authorized to validate a message was unable to do so because the message was corrupted or altered. This may be useful as a permanent, transient persistent, or successful delivery code.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: This response to the AUTH command indicates that the authentication failed due to invalid or insufficient authentication credentials. In this case, the client SHOULD ask the user to supply new credentials (such as by presenting a password dialog box).
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: This response to the AUTH command indicates that the selected authentication mechanism is weaker than server policy permits for that user. The client SHOULD retry with a new authentication mechanism.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: This indicates that external strong privacy layer is needed in order to use the requested authentication mechanism. This is primarily intended for use with clear text authentication mechanisms. A client which receives this may activate a security layer such as TLS prior to authenticating, or attempt to use a stronger mechanism.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.sample: Encryption required for requested authentication mechanism
enhanced.desc: This response to the AUTH command indicates that the selected authentication mechanism may only be used when the underlying SMTP connection is encrypted. Note that this response code is documented here for historical purposes only. Modern implementations SHOULD NOT advertise mechanisms that are not permitted due to lack of encryption, unless an encryption layer of sufficient strength is currently being employed.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: This response to the AUTH command indicates that the user needs to transition to the selected authentication mechanism. This is typically done by authenticating once using the [PLAIN] authentication mechanism. The selected mechanism SHOULD then work for authentications in subsequent sessions.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: Sometimes a system administrator will have to disable a user's account (e.g., due to lack of payment, abuse, evidence of a break-in attempt, etc). This error code occurs after a successful authentication to a disabled account. This informs the client that the failure is permanent until the user contacts their system administrator to get the account re-enabled. It differs from a generic authentication failure where the client's best option is to present the passphrase entry dialog in case the user simply mistyped their passphrase.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: The submission server requires a configured trust relationship with a third-party server in order to access the message content. This value replaces the prior use of X.7.8 for this error condition. thereby updating [RFC4468].
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: The specified priority level is below the lowest priority acceptable for the receiving SMTP server. This condition might be temporary, for example the server is operating in a mode where only higher priority messages are accepted for transfer and delivery, while lower priority messages are rejected.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.sample: Message is too big for the specified priority
enhanced.desc: The message is too big for the specified priority. This condition might be temporary, for example the server is operating in a mode where only higher priority messages below certain size are accepted for transfer and delivery.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when a message is received with a Require-Recipient-Valid-Since field or RRVS extension and the receiving system is able to determine that the intended recipient mailbox has not been under continuous ownership since the specified date-time.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when a message is received with a Require-Recipient-Valid-Since field or RRVS extension and the receiving system wishes to disclose that the owner of the domain name of the recipient has changed since the specified date-time.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when a message is received with a Require-Recipient-Valid-Since field or RRVS extension and the receiving system cannot complete the requested evaluation because the required timestamp was not recorded. The message originator needs to decide whether to reissue the message without RRVS protection.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when a message did not contain any passing DKIM signatures. (This violates the advice of Section 6.1 of [RFC6376].)
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when a message contains one or more passing DKIM signatures, but none are acceptable. (This violates the advice of Section 6.1 of [RFC6376].)
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.sample: No valid author-matched DKIM signature found
enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when a message contains one or more passing DKIM signatures, but none are acceptable because none have an identifier(s) that matches the author address(es) found in the From header field. This is a special case of X.7.21. (This violates the advice of Section 6.1 of [RFC6376].)
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when a message completed an SPF check that produced a "fail" result, contrary to local policy requirements. Used in place of 5.7.1 as described in Section 8.4 of [RFC7208].
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when evaluation of SPF relative to an arriving message resulted in an error. Used in place of 4.4.3 or 5.5.2 as described in Sections 8.6 and 8.7 of [RFC7208].
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when an SMTP client's IP address failed a reverse DNS validation check, contrary to local policy requirements.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when a message failed more than one message authentication check, contrary to local policy requirements. The particular mechanisms that failed are not specified.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when the associated sender address has a null MX, and the SMTP receiver is configured to reject mail from such sender (e.g., because it could not return a DSN).
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: The message appears to be part of a mail flood of similar abusive messages.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: This status code may be returned when a message fails ARC validation.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: This indicates that the message was not able to be forwarded because it was received with a REQUIRETLS requirement and none of the SMTP servers to which the message should be forwarded provide this support.
enhanced.note: A policy or reputation decision, held open rather than refused. Slow down for this provider and read the text.

enhanced.desc: Other undefined status is the only undefined error code. It should be used for all errors for which only the class of the error is known.
enhanced.note: Permanent and unspecified. The accompanying text is the only evidence.

enhanced.desc: Something about the address specified in the message caused this DSN.
enhanced.note: The address is wrong or gone. Remove it; retrying costs reputation.

enhanced.desc: The mailbox specified in the address does not exist. For Internet mail names, this means the address portion to the left of the "@" sign is invalid. This code is only useful for permanent failures.
enhanced.note: The mailbox does not exist. Permanent. Suppress immediately: repeated delivery to unknown users is the fastest way to lose reputation at any provider.

enhanced.desc: The destination system specified in the address does not exist or is incapable of accepting mail. For Internet mail names, this means the address portion to the right of the "@" is invalid for mail. This code is only useful for permanent failures.
enhanced.note: The destination domain does not exist or takes no mail. Check for a typo in the domain, then suppress.

enhanced.desc: The destination address was syntactically invalid. This can apply to any field in the address. This code is only useful for permanent failures.
enhanced.note: The address is wrong or gone. Remove it; retrying costs reputation.

enhanced.desc: The mailbox address as specified matches one or more recipients on the destination system. This may result if a heuristic address mapping algorithm is used to map the specified address to a local mailbox name.
enhanced.note: The address is wrong or gone. Remove it; retrying costs reputation.

enhanced.desc: This mailbox address as specified was valid. This status code should be used for positive delivery reports.
enhanced.note: The address is wrong or gone. Remove it; retrying costs reputation.

enhanced.sample: Destination mailbox has moved, No forwarding address
enhanced.desc: The mailbox address provided was at one time valid, but mail is no longer being accepted for that address. This code is only useful for permanent failures.
enhanced.note: The mailbox has moved and no forwarding address was given.

enhanced.desc: The sender's address was syntactically invalid. This can apply to any field in the address.
enhanced.note: The address is wrong or gone. Remove it; retrying costs reputation.

enhanced.desc: The sender's system specified in the address does not exist or is incapable of accepting return mail. For domain names, this means the address portion to the right of the "@" is invalid for mail.
enhanced.note: Your envelope sender is bad. This is your configuration, not the recipient's mailbox.

enhanced.desc: The mailbox address specified was valid, but the message has been relayed to a system that does not speak this protocol; no further information can be provided.
enhanced.note: The address is wrong or gone. Remove it; retrying costs reputation.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when the associated address is marked as invalid using a null MX.
enhanced.note: The address is wrong or gone. Remove it; retrying costs reputation.

enhanced.desc: The mailbox exists, but something about the destination mailbox has caused the sending of this DSN.
enhanced.note: The mailbox will not take mail. Suppress it, because dormant addresses become spam traps.

enhanced.desc: The mailbox exists, but is not accepting messages. This may be a permanent error if the mailbox will never be re-enabled or a transient error if the mailbox is only temporarily disabled.
enhanced.note: The mailbox is disabled or not accepting mail. Suppress: these turn into spam traps.

enhanced.desc: The mailbox is full because the user has exceeded a per-mailbox administrative quota or physical capacity. The general semantics implies that the recipient can delete messages to make more space available. This code should be used as a persistent transient failure.
enhanced.note: Over quota, permanently signalled. Some receivers use 5.2.2 where others use 4.2.2, so retry a few times before suppressing.

enhanced.desc: A per-mailbox administrative message length limit has been exceeded. This status code should be used when the per-mailbox message length limit is less than the general system limit. This code should be used as a permanent failure.
enhanced.note: The message is too large for the mailbox. Reduce the message size.

enhanced.desc: The mailbox is a mailing list address and the mailing list was unable to be expanded. This code may represent a permanent failure or a persistent transient failure.
enhanced.note: The mailbox will not take mail. Suppress it, because dormant addresses become spam traps.

enhanced.sample: Other or undefined mail system status
enhanced.desc: The destination system exists and normally accepts mail, but something about the system has caused the generation of this DSN.
enhanced.note: The receiving system refused it outright. Usually message size or a system limit.

enhanced.desc: Mail system storage has been exceeded. The general semantics imply that the individual recipient may not be able to delete material to make room for additional messages. This is useful only as a persistent transient error.
enhanced.note: The receiving system refused it outright. Usually message size or a system limit.

enhanced.desc: The host on which the mailbox is resident is not accepting messages. Examples of such conditions include an imminent shutdown, excessive load, or system maintenance. This is useful for both permanent and persistent transient errors.
enhanced.note: The receiving system refused it outright. Usually message size or a system limit.

enhanced.sample: System not capable of selected features
enhanced.desc: Selected features specified for the message are not supported by the destination system. This can occur in gateways when features from one domain cannot be mapped onto the supported feature in another.
enhanced.note: The receiving system refused it outright. Usually message size or a system limit.

enhanced.desc: The message is larger than per-message size limit. This limit may either be for physical or administrative reasons. This is useful only as a permanent error.
enhanced.note: The message is too large for the system. Check your maximum message size against the receiver's.

enhanced.desc: The system is not configured in a manner that will permit it to accept this message.
enhanced.note: The receiving system refused it outright. Usually message size or a system limit.

enhanced.desc: The message was accepted for relay/delivery, but the requested priority (possibly the implied default) was not honoured. The human readable text after the status code contains the new priority, followed by SP (space) and explanatory human readable text.
enhanced.note: The receiving system refused it outright. Usually message size or a system limit.

enhanced.sample: Other or undefined network or routing status
enhanced.desc: Something went wrong with the networking, but it is not clear what the problem is, or the problem cannot be well expressed with any of the other provided detail codes.
enhanced.note: Permanent routing failure. Check the destination's DNS before blaming the address.

enhanced.desc: The outbound connection attempt was not answered, because either the remote system was busy, or was unable to take a call. This is useful only as a persistent transient error.
enhanced.note: No answer from the destination and no route to it. Verify the domain's MX records exist and resolve.

enhanced.desc: The outbound connection was established, but was unable to complete the message transaction, either because of time-out, or inadequate connection quality. This is useful only as a persistent transient error.
enhanced.note: Permanent routing failure. Check the destination's DNS before blaming the address.

enhanced.desc: The network system was unable to forward the message, because a directory server was unavailable. This is useful only as a persistent transient error. The inability to connect to an Internet DNS server is one example of the directory server failure error.
enhanced.note: Permanent routing failure. Check the destination's DNS before blaming the address.

enhanced.desc: The mail system was unable to determine the next hop for the message because the necessary routing information was unavailable from the directory server. This is useful for both permanent and persistent transient errors. A DNS lookup returning only an SOA (Start of Administration) record for a domain name is one example of the unable to route error.
enhanced.note: Unable to route. Usually a DNS problem at the destination.

enhanced.desc: The mail system was unable to deliver the message because the mail system was congested. This is useful only as a persistent transient error.
enhanced.note: Permanent routing failure. Check the destination's DNS before blaming the address.

enhanced.desc: A routing loop caused the message to be forwarded too many times, either because of incorrect routing tables or a user- forwarding loop. This is useful only as a persistent transient error.
enhanced.note: Permanent routing failure. Check the destination's DNS before blaming the address.

enhanced.desc: The message was considered too old by the rejecting system, either because it remained on that host too long or because the time-to-live value specified by the sender of the message was exceeded. If possible, the code for the actual problem found when delivery was attempted should be returned rather than this code.
enhanced.note: Permanent routing failure. Check the destination's DNS before blaming the address.

enhanced.desc: Something was wrong with the protocol necessary to deliver the message to the next hop and the problem cannot be well expressed with any of the other provided detail codes.
enhanced.note: The SMTP conversation went wrong. Check what your MTA sent immediately before this.

enhanced.desc: A mail transaction protocol command was issued which was either out of sequence or unsupported. This is useful only as a permanent error.
enhanced.note: A protocol error. Something in how the message or session is constructed is wrong.

enhanced.desc: A mail transaction protocol command was issued which could not be interpreted, either because the syntax was wrong or the command is unrecognized. This is useful only as a permanent error.
enhanced.note: A protocol error. Something in how the message or session is constructed is wrong.

enhanced.desc: More recipients were specified for the message than could have been delivered by the protocol. This error should normally result in the segmentation of the message into two, the remainder of the recipients to be delivered on a subsequent delivery attempt. It is included in this list in the event that such segmentation is not possible.
enhanced.note: A protocol error. Something in how the message or session is constructed is wrong.

enhanced.desc: A valid mail transaction protocol command was issued with invalid arguments, either because the arguments were out of range or represented unrecognized features. This is useful only as a permanent error.
enhanced.note: A protocol error. Something in how the message or session is constructed is wrong.

enhanced.desc: A protocol version mis-match existed which could not be automatically resolved by the communicating parties.
enhanced.note: A protocol error. Something in how the message or session is constructed is wrong.

enhanced.sample: Authentication Exchange line is too long
enhanced.desc: This enhanced status code SHOULD be returned when the server fails the AUTH command due to the client sending a [BASE64] response which is longer than the maximum buffer size available for the currently selected SASL mechanism. This is useful for both permanent and persistent transient errors.
enhanced.note: A protocol error. Something in how the message or session is constructed is wrong.

enhanced.desc: Something about the content of a message caused it to be considered undeliverable and the problem cannot be well expressed with any of the other provided detail codes.
enhanced.note: The content was refused. Change the message, not the rate.

enhanced.desc: The media of the message is not supported by either the delivery protocol or the next system in the forwarding path. This is useful only as a permanent error.
enhanced.note: The content was refused. Change the message, not the rate.

enhanced.desc: The content of the message must be converted before it can be delivered and such conversion is not permitted. Such prohibitions may be the expression of the sender in the message itself or the policy of the sending host.
enhanced.note: The content was refused. Change the message, not the rate.

enhanced.desc: The message content must be converted in order to be forwarded but such conversion is not possible or is not practical by a host in the forwarding path. This condition may result when an ESMTP gateway supports 8bit transport but is not able to downgrade the message to 7 bit as required for the next hop.
enhanced.note: The content was refused. Change the message, not the rate.

enhanced.desc: This is a warning sent to the sender when message delivery was successfully but when the delivery required a conversion in which some data was lost. This may also be a permanent error if the sender has indicated that conversion with loss is prohibited for the message.
enhanced.note: The content was refused. Change the message, not the rate.

enhanced.desc: A conversion was required but was unsuccessful. This may be useful as a permanent or persistent temporary notification.
enhanced.note: The content was refused. Change the message, not the rate.

enhanced.desc: The message content could not be fetched from a remote system. This may be useful as a permanent or persistent temporary notification.
enhanced.note: The content was refused. Change the message, not the rate.

enhanced.sample: Non-ASCII addresses not permitted for that sender/recipient
enhanced.desc: This indicates the reception of a MAIL or RCPT command that non-ASCII addresses are not permitted
enhanced.note: The content was refused. Change the message, not the rate.

enhanced.sample: UTF-8 string reply is required, but not permitted by the SMTP client
enhanced.desc: This indicates that a reply containing a UTF-8 string is required to show the mailbox name, but that form of response is not permitted by the SMTP client.
enhanced.note: The content was refused. Change the message, not the rate.

enhanced.sample: UTF-8 header message cannot be transferred to one or more recipients, so the message must be rejected
enhanced.desc: This indicates that transaction failed after the final "." of the DATA command.
enhanced.note: The content was refused. Change the message, not the rate.

enhanced.desc: This is a duplicate of X.6.8 and is thus deprecated.
enhanced.note: The content was refused. Change the message, not the rate.

enhanced.desc: Something related to security caused the message to be returned, and the problem cannot be well expressed with any of the other provided detail codes. This status code may also be used when the condition cannot be further described because of security policies in force.
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.desc: The sender is not authorized to send to the destination. This can be the result of per-host or per-recipient filtering. This memo does not discuss the merits of any such filtering, but provides a mechanism to report such. This is useful only as a permanent error.
enhanced.note: Delivery not authorised. This covers everything from a reputation block to a relaying refusal, so the accompanying text decides what it actually is.

enhanced.desc: The sender is not authorized to send a message to the intended mailing list. This is useful only as a permanent error.
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.sample: Security conversion required but not possible
enhanced.desc: A conversion from one secure messaging protocol to another was required for delivery and such conversion was not possible. This is useful only as a permanent error.
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.desc: A message contained security features such as secure authentication that could not be supported on the delivery protocol. This is useful only as a permanent error.
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.desc: A transport system otherwise authorized to validate or decrypt a message in transport was unable to do so because necessary information such as key was not available or such information was invalid.
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.desc: A transport system otherwise authorized to validate or decrypt a message was unable to do so because the necessary algorithm was not supported.
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.desc: A transport system otherwise authorized to validate a message was unable to do so because the message was corrupted or altered. This may be useful as a permanent, transient persistent, or successful delivery code.
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.desc: This response to the AUTH command indicates that the authentication failed due to invalid or insufficient authentication credentials. In this case, the client SHOULD ask the user to supply new credentials (such as by presenting a password dialog box).
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.desc: This response to the AUTH command indicates that the selected authentication mechanism is weaker than server policy permits for that user. The client SHOULD retry with a new authentication mechanism.
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.desc: This indicates that external strong privacy layer is needed in order to use the requested authentication mechanism. This is primarily intended for use with clear text authentication mechanisms. A client which receives this may activate a security layer such as TLS prior to authenticating, or attempt to use a stronger mechanism.
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.sample: Encryption required for requested authentication mechanism
enhanced.desc: This response to the AUTH command indicates that the selected authentication mechanism may only be used when the underlying SMTP connection is encrypted. Note that this response code is documented here for historical purposes only. Modern implementations SHOULD NOT advertise mechanisms that are not permitted due to lack of encryption, unless an encryption layer of sufficient strength is currently being employed.
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.desc: This response to the AUTH command indicates that the user needs to transition to the selected authentication mechanism. This is typically done by authenticating once using the [PLAIN] authentication mechanism. The selected mechanism SHOULD then work for authentications in subsequent sessions.
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.desc: Sometimes a system administrator will have to disable a user's account (e.g., due to lack of payment, abuse, evidence of a break-in attempt, etc). This error code occurs after a successful authentication to a disabled account. This informs the client that the failure is permanent until the user contacts their system administrator to get the account re-enabled. It differs from a generic authentication failure where the client's best option is to present the passphrase entry dialog in case the user simply mistyped their passphrase.
enhanced.note: The sending account is disabled. This is your side.

enhanced.desc: The submission server requires a configured trust relationship with a third-party server in order to access the message content. This value replaces the prior use of X.7.8 for this error condition. thereby updating [RFC4468].
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.desc: The specified priority level is below the lowest priority acceptable for the receiving SMTP server. This condition might be temporary, for example the server is operating in a mode where only higher priority messages are accepted for transfer and delivery, while lower priority messages are rejected.
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.sample: Message is too big for the specified priority
enhanced.desc: The message is too big for the specified priority. This condition might be temporary, for example the server is operating in a mode where only higher priority messages below certain size are accepted for transfer and delivery.
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when a message is received with a Require-Recipient-Valid-Since field or RRVS extension and the receiving system is able to determine that the intended recipient mailbox has not been under continuous ownership since the specified date-time.
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when a message is received with a Require-Recipient-Valid-Since field or RRVS extension and the receiving system wishes to disclose that the owner of the domain name of the recipient has changed since the specified date-time.
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when a message is received with a Require-Recipient-Valid-Since field or RRVS extension and the receiving system cannot complete the requested evaluation because the required timestamp was not recorded. The message originator needs to decide whether to reissue the message without RRVS protection.
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when a message did not contain any passing DKIM signatures. (This violates the advice of Section 6.1 of [RFC6376].)
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when a message contains one or more passing DKIM signatures, but none are acceptable. (This violates the advice of Section 6.1 of [RFC6376].)
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.sample: No valid author-matched DKIM signature found
enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when a message contains one or more passing DKIM signatures, but none are acceptable because none have an identifier(s) that matches the author address(es) found in the From header field. This is a special case of X.7.21. (This violates the advice of Section 6.1 of [RFC6376].)
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when a message completed an SPF check that produced a "fail" result, contrary to local policy requirements. Used in place of 5.7.1 as described in Section 8.4 of [RFC7208].
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when evaluation of SPF relative to an arriving message resulted in an error. Used in place of 4.4.3 or 5.5.2 as described in Sections 8.6 and 8.7 of [RFC7208].
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when an SMTP client's IP address failed a reverse DNS validation check, contrary to local policy requirements.
enhanced.note: The reverse DNS of your sending IP does not resolve forward to the same address. Fix rDNS and the forward record.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when a message failed more than one message authentication check, contrary to local policy requirements. The particular mechanisms that failed are not specified.
enhanced.note: Authentication failed under the domain's DMARC policy. Retrying will not help; SPF or DKIM has to pass and align.

enhanced.desc: This status code is returned when the associated sender address has a null MX, and the SMTP receiver is configured to reject mail from such sender (e.g., because it could not return a DSN).
enhanced.note: The sender domain has no MX record. Nothing can reply to it.

enhanced.desc: The message appears to be part of a mail flood of similar abusive messages.
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.desc: This status code may be returned when a message fails ARC validation.
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

enhanced.desc: This indicates that the message was not able to be forwarded because it was received with a REQUIRETLS requirement and none of the SMTP servers to which the message should be forwarded provide this support.
enhanced.note: A security or policy refusal. Stop and read the text before sending more.

provider.text: Unusual rate of unsolicited mail from your IP
Server busy, please try again later
Internal reason code attached to an IP reputation block
Internal reason code attached to an IP reputation block
Deferred for policy or reputation reasons

microsoft.sample: Message expired
microsoft.why: The message in the queue expired. The sending server tried to relay or deliver the message, but the action wasn't completed before the message expiration time. This message can also indicate that a message header limit was reached on a remote server, or some other protocol timeout occurred during server communication.
microsoft.fix: This message usually indicates an issue on the receiving server. Check the validity of the recipient address, and determine whether the receiving server is configured correctly to receive messages. You might have to reduce the number of recipients in the message header for the host about which you're receiving this error. If you send the message again, the message is placed in the queue again. If the receiving server is available, the message is delivered. For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 4.4.7 in Exchange Online.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: MX hosts of <domain> failed MTA-STS validation
microsoft.why: The destination MX host isn't the expected host per the domain's Strict Transport Security (STS) policy.
microsoft.fix: This error usually indicates that the destination domain's MTA-STS policy doesn't contain the MX host. For more information, see Enhancing mail flow with MTA-STS.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Connection refused [Message=Socket error code 10061]
microsoft.why: Microsoft 365 is trying to send a message to an email server outside Microsoft 365, but all attempts to connect are failing because of a network connection issue at the external server's location.
microsoft.fix: This error almost always indicates an issue that affects the receiving server or network outside of Microsoft 365. The error should also include the IP address of the server or service that's generating the error. You can use this address to identify the party that's responsible for fixing this issue.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Too many recipients
microsoft.why: The message has more than 200 SMTP envelope recipients from the same domain.
microsoft.fix: An envelope recipient is the original, unexpanded recipient that's used in the RCPT TO command to transmit the message between SMTP servers. If Microsoft 365 returns this error, the sending server must break up the number of envelope recipients into smaller chunks (chunking) and resend the message.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Remote certificate failed MTA-STS validation. Reason: <validityStatus>
microsoft.why: The destination mail server's certificate must chain to a trusted root Certificate Authority and the Common Name or Subject Alternative Name must contain an entry for the host name in the STS policy.
microsoft.fix: This error usually indicates an issue with the destination mail server's certificate. For more information, see Enhancing mail flow with MTA-STS.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Access denied, a message sent over IPv6 [2a01:111:f200:2004::240] must pass either SPF or DKIM validation, this message is not signed
microsoft.why: The sending message sent over IPv6 must pass either SPF or DKIM.
microsoft.fix: For more information, see Support for anonymous inbound email messages over IPv6.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: starttls-not-supported: Destination mail server must support TLS to receive mail.
microsoft.why: - DNSSEC checks passed. However, upon establishing the connection, the destination mail server doesn't respond to the STARTTLS command. - The destination server responds to the STARTTLS command, but the TLS handshake fails.
microsoft.fix: This message usually indicates an issue on the destination email server. Check the validity of the recipient address. Determine whether the destination server is configured correctly to receive the messages.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: certificate-expired: Destination mail server's certificate is expired.
microsoft.why: DNSSEC checks passed. However, upon establishing the connection, the destination mail server provides an expired certificate.
microsoft.fix: A valid X.509 certificate that isn't expired must be presented. X.509 certificates must be renewed after their expiration, most commonly on an annual basis.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: tlsa-invalid: The domain failed DANE validation.
microsoft.why: Records are DNSSEC authentic, but one or multiple of these scenarios occurred: - The destination mail server's certificate doesn't match the authentic TLSA record requirements. - Authentic TLSA record is misconfigured. - Destination domain is being attacked. - Any other DANE failure.
microsoft.fix: This message usually indicates an issue on the destination email server. Check the validity of the recipient address and determine whether the destination server is configured correctly to receive messages. For more information, see DANE protocol: updates and operational guidance.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: dnssec-invalid: Destination domain returned invalid DNSSEC records
microsoft.why: The destination domain indicated that it was DNSSEC-authentic, but Exchange Online wasn't able to verify it as DNSSEC-authentic.
microsoft.fix: For more information, see Overview of DNSSEC.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: certificate-host-mismatch: Remote certificate MUST have a common name or subject alternative name that matches the hostname (DANE)
microsoft.why: This error occurs if the presented certificate identities (CN and SAN) of a destination SMTP target host don't match any of the domains or MX host.
microsoft.fix: This message usually indicates an issue on the destination email server. Check the validity of the recipient address and determine whether the destination server is configured correctly to receive messages. For more information, see How SMTP DNS-based Authentication of Named Entities (DANE) works to secure email communications.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Access denied, please try again later
microsoft.why: Suspicious activity was detected and sending was temporarily restricted for further evaluation.
microsoft.fix: If this activity is valid, this restriction is lifted shortly.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Access denied, please try again later
microsoft.why: Suspicious activity was detected on the IP in question, and the address is temporarily restricted while being further evaluated.
microsoft.fix: If this activity is valid, this restriction is lifted shortly.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Generic error, x-dg-ref header is too long, or Requested action not taken: policy violation detected (AS345)
microsoft.why: 5.0.350 is a generic catch-all error code for a wide variety of nonspecific errors from the recipient's email organization. The specific x-dg-ref header is too long message is related to Rich Text-formatted messages. The specific Requested action not taken: policy violation detected (AS345) message is related to nested attachments.
microsoft.fix: For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 550 5.0.350 in Exchange Online.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Sender denied
microsoft.why: This NDR commonly occurs when someone saves an email message to a file in Outlook, opens it offline, and then replies. The message property preserves only the legacyExchangeDN attribute when Outlook delivers the message. Therefore, the lookup could fail.
microsoft.fix: Either the recipient address is incorrectly formatted or the recipient couldn't be correctly resolved. The first step to resolve this error is to check the recipient address, and send the message again. For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.1.0 in Exchange Online.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Bad destination mailbox address
microsoft.why: The following conditions might cause this failure: - The sender incorrectly entered the recipient's email address. - The recipient's email address doesn't exist in the destination email system. - The recipient's mailbox was moved, and the sender’s Outlook recipient cache didn't update. - An invalid legacy domain name (DN) exists for the recipient's mailbox Active Directory Domain Service.
microsoft.fix: This error typically occurs if the sender of the message enters an incorrect email address of the recipient. The sender should check the recipient's email address and send again. This error can occur if the recipient’s email address was previously valid but later changed or removed. If the sender of the message is in the same organization as the recipient, and the recipient's mailbox still exists, determine whether the recipient's mailbox was relocated to a new email server. If so, Outlook might not update the recipient cache correctly. Instruct the sender to remove the recipient's address from sender's Outlook recipient cache, and then create a new message. Resending the original message causes the same failure. For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.1.1 through 5.1.20 in Exchange Online.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Access denied, bad outbound sender
microsoft.why: The account was blocked for sending too much spam. Typically, this problem occurs because the account was compromised (hacked) by phishing or malware.
microsoft.fix: For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.1.8 in Exchange Online.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Recipient not found
microsoft.why: SMTP address lookup didn't find the recipient's <SMTP Address>.
microsoft.fix: For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 550 5.1.10 in Exchange Online.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Your message can't be sent because you've reached your daily limit for message recipients
microsoft.why: The sender exceeded the recipient rate limit, as described in Sending limits.
microsoft.fix: This error could indicate that the account was compromised and is being used to send spam. For more information, see Responding to a compromised account.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Submission quota exceeded
microsoft.why: The sender exceeded the recipient rate limit or the message rate limit as described in Sending limits.
microsoft.fix: This error could indicate the account was compromised and is being used to send spam. For more information, see Responding to a compromised account.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Recipient's per hour message receive limit from specific sender exceeded
microsoft.why: The sender exceeded the maximum number of messages that they're allowed to send per hour to a specific recipient in Exchange Online.
microsoft.fix: The automated mailer or sender should try again later, and reduce the number of messages that they send per hour to a specific recipient. This limit helps protect Microsoft 365 and Office 365 users from rapidly filling their Inboxes with many messages from errant automated notification systems or other single-sender mail storms. The "Mailboxes exceeding receiving limits" report shows detailed information about the mailboxes that are receiving large volumes of messages in a short time.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Recipient's per hour message receive limit exceeded
microsoft.why: The Microsoft 365 recipient exceeded the number of messages that they can receive per hour from all senders.
microsoft.fix: The automated mailer or sender should try again later, and reduce the number of messages that they send per hour to a specific recipient. This limit helps protect Microsoft 365 and Office 365 users from rapidly filling their Inboxes with many messages from errant automated notification systems or other mail storms. The "Mailboxes exceeding receiving limits" report shows detailed information about the mailboxes that are receiving large volumes of messages in a short time.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Journaling on-premises messages to Microsoft 365 not supported when Journaling Archive is disabled
microsoft.why: Journaling on‑premises messages to Microsoft 365 isn’t supported for this organization because Journaling Archive isn’t enabled in the organization’s settings.
microsoft.fix: A journaling rule is configured in the organization's on-premises environment to journal on-premises messages to Microsoft 365, but Journaling Archive is disabled. For this scenario to work, the organization's Office 365 administrator should either enable Journaling Archive or change the journaling rule to journal messages to a different location.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Relay Access Denied
microsoft.why: The mail server that's generating the error doesn't accept mail for the recipient's domain. Mail server or DNS misconfiguration causes this error.
microsoft.fix: For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.4.1 in Exchange Online.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Recipient address rejected: Access denied
microsoft.why: The recipient's address doesn't exist.
microsoft.fix: For more information, see Use Directory Based Edge Blocking to reject messages sent to invalid recipients.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: MX hosts of <domain> failed MTA-STS validation
microsoft.why: The destination MX host wasn't the host expected per the domain's STS policy.
microsoft.fix: This error usually indicates that the destination domain's MTA-STS policy doesn't contain the MX host. For more information, see Enhancing mail flow with MTA-STS.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Message expired
microsoft.why: The email message wasn't delivered in time. The destination server didn't respond, or an error occurred, and the NDR could not be delivered to the sender.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: 550 5.5.0 Requested action not taken: mailbox unavailable
microsoft.why: The recipient's <SMTP Address> domain is @hotmail.com or @outlook.com and it wasn't found by SMTP address lookup.
microsoft.fix: Similar to 550 5.1.10. For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 550 5.1.10 in Exchange Online.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Invalid characters
microsoft.why: Your email program added invalid characters (bare line feed characters) to a message that you sent.
microsoft.fix: For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.6.11 in Exchange Online.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Delivery not authorized
microsoft.why: The sender of the message isn't allowed to send messages to the recipient.
microsoft.fix: This error occurs if the sender tries to send a message to a recipient but the sender isn't authorized to send one. This error frequently occurs when a sender tries to send messages to a distribution group that's configured to accept messages only from members of that distribution group or other authorized senders. The sender must request permission to send messages to the recipient. This error can also occur if an Exchange transport rule rejects a message because the message matched conditions that are configured on the transport rule. For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.1 in Exchange Online.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Unable to relay
microsoft.why: The sending email system isn't allowed to send a message to an email system that isn't the final destination of the message.
microsoft.fix: This error occurs if the sending email system tries to send an anonymous message to a receiving email system, and the receiving email system doesn't accept messages for the domain or domains that are specified in one or more of the recipients. The following are the most common cause of this error: - A third party tries to use a receiving email system to send spam, and the receiving email system rejects the attempt. By the nature of spam, the sender's email address might be forged, and the resulting NDR could have been sent to the unsuspecting sender's email address. It's difficult to avoid this situation. - An MX record for a domain points to a receiving email system where that domain isn't accepted. The administrator responsible for the specific domain name must correct the MX record or configure the receiving email system to accept messages sent to that domain, or do both. - A sending email system or client that should use the receiving email system to relay messages doesn't have the correct permissions to do this. For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.1 in Exchange Online.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Client was not authenticated
microsoft.why: The sending email system didn't authenticate with the receiving email system. The receiving email system requires authentication before message submission.
microsoft.fix: This error occurs if the receiving server must be authenticated before message submission, and the sending email system isn't authenticated with the receiving email system. The sending email system administrator must configure the sending email system to authenticate with the receiving email system for delivery to be successful. For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.1 in Exchange Online.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Remote certificate failed MTA-STS validation. Reason: <validityStatus>
microsoft.why: The destination mail server's certificate must chain to a trusted root Certificate Authority and the Common Name or Subject Alternative Name must contain an entry for the host name in the STS policy.
microsoft.fix: This error usually indicates an issue with the destination mail server's certificate. For more information, see Enhancing mail flow with MTA-STS.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Sender was not authenticated by organization
microsoft.why: The sender's message is rejected because the recipient address is set up to reject messages sent from outside its organization. Only an email administrator for the recipient's organization can change this configuration.
microsoft.fix: For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.12 in Exchange Online.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: The message was rejected because of Sender Policy Framework violation
microsoft.why: The destination email system uses SPF to validate inbound mail, and an issue affects your SPF configuration.
microsoft.fix: For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.23 in Exchange Online.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Access denied, the sending IPv6 address [2a01:111:f200:2004::240] must have a reverse DNS record
microsoft.why: The sending IPv6 address must have a reverse DNS record to send email over IPv6.
microsoft.fix: For more information, see Support for anonymous inbound email messages over IPv6.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Client was not authenticated to send anonymous mail during MAIL FROM
microsoft.why: You configured an application or device to send (relay) email messages in Microsoft 365 using the smtp.office365.com endpoint, and an issue affects the configuration of the application or device.
microsoft.fix: For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.57 in Exchange Online.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: TenantAttribution; Relay Access Denied
microsoft.why: You use an inbound connector to receive messages from your on-premises email environment, and something changed in your on-premises environment that makes the inbound connector's configuration incorrect.
microsoft.fix: For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.64 in Exchange Online.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Sender not in allowed-senders list
microsoft.why: The sender doesn't have permission to send to the distribution group because the sender isn't in the group's allowed-senders list. Depending how the group is set up, even the group's owner might have to be added to the allowed sender list in order to send messages to the group.
microsoft.fix: For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.124 in Exchange Online.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Sender not authenticated for group
microsoft.why: The recipient address is a group distribution list that's set up to reject messages sent from outside its organization. Only an email administrator for the recipient's organization or the group owner can change this configuration.
microsoft.fix: For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.133 in Exchange Online.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Sender was not authenticated for mailbox
microsoft.why: The recipient address is a mailbox that's set up to reject messages sent from outside its organization. Only an email administrator for the recipient's organization can change this configuration.
microsoft.fix: For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.134 in Exchange Online.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Sender was not authenticated
microsoft.why: The recipient address is a mail user that's set up to reject messages sent from outside its organization. Only an email administrator for the recipient's organization can change this configuration.
microsoft.fix: For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.136 in Exchange Online.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Your message can't be sent because your trial tenant has exceeded its daily limit for sending email to external recipients (tenant external recipient rate limit)
microsoft.why: The number of external recipients emailed in a 24-hour period exceeds the external recipient rate limit in Exchange Online. The limit applies per trial tenant.
microsoft.fix: The external recipient rate limit is tracked over a 24-hour rolling window.
