When the count for the most recent 24-hour period falls below the limit, users in the trial tenant can resume sending messages to external recipients. The limit helps prevent the distribution of unsolicited bulk messages.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Your message can't be sent because your tenant exceeded its daily limit for sending email to external recipients (tenant external recipient rate limit)
microsoft.why: The number of external recipients emailed in a 24-hour period exceeds the external recipient rate limit in Exchange Online. The limit applies per tenant.
microsoft.fix: The external recipient rate limit is tracked over a 24-hour rolling window. When the count for the most recent 24-hour period falls below the limit, users in the tenant can resume sending messages to external recipients. The limit helps prevent the distribution of unsolicited bulk messages.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Your message can't be sent because your tenant has exceeded its daily limit for sending email to external recipients from your tenant's onmicrosoft.com domains
microsoft.why: Your organization exceeded the limit of sending emails to 100 external recipients from your organization’s onmicrosoft.com (MOERA) domain within a 24‑hour rolling window. This limit is enforced per tenant.
microsoft.fix: MOERA (onmicrosoft.com) domains are intended only for testing, and shouldn't be used to send regular email messages. Messages sent from these domains are limited to 100 external recipients for a rolling 24-hour period. Inbound emails aren't affected. External recipients are counted after any recipient list expansion. To avoid this limit, purchase and migrate to a custom domain. Then, make sure that only the custom domain is used to send email messages to external recipients.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: starttls-not-supported: Destination mail server must support TLS to receive mail.
microsoft.why: - DNSSEC checks passed. However, upon establishing the connection, the destination mail server doesn't respond to the STARTTLS command. - The destination server responds to the STARTTLS command, but the TLS handshake fails.
microsoft.fix: This message usually indicates an issue on the destination mail server. Check the validity of the recipient address and determine if the destination server is configured correctly to receive messages.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: certificate-expired: Destination mail server's certificate is expired.
microsoft.why: DNSSEC checks passed. However, upon establishing the connection, the destination mail server provides a certificate that's expired.
microsoft.fix: A valid X.509 certificate that isn't expired must be presented. X.509 certificates must be renewed after their expiration, most commonly on an annual basis.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: tlsa-invalid: The domain failed DANE validation.
microsoft.why: Records are DNSSEC authentic but one or more of the following things occurred: - The destination mail server's certificate doesn't match what is expected per the authentic TLSA record. - The authentic TLSA record is misconfigured. - The destination domain is being attacked. - The certificate start date is in the future. - Any other DANE failure.
microsoft.fix: This message usually indicates an issue exists on the destination mail server. Check the validity of the recipient address and determine if the destination server is configured correctly to receive messages. For more information about DANE, see https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7671.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: dnssec-invalid: Destination domain returned invalid DNSSEC records
microsoft.why: The destination domain indicated it was DNSSEC authentic but Exchange Online wasn't able to verify it as DNSSEC authentic.
microsoft.fix: For more information about DNSSEC, see Overview of DNSSEC.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: certificate-host-mismatch: Remote certificate MUST have a common name or subject alternative name matching the hostname (DANE)
microsoft.why: This error occurs if the presented certificate identities (CN and SAN) of a destination SMTP target host don't match any of the domains or MX host.
microsoft.fix: This message usually indicates an issue on the destination email server. Check the validity of recipient address and determine whether the destination server is configured correctly to receive messages. For more information, see How SMTP DNS-based Authentication of Named Entities (DANE) works to secure email communications.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Remote server returned not permitted to relay
microsoft.why: This error occurs because of SPF or DKIM authentication failures in forwarded or relayed emails. This problem occurs more frequently in mail flows that include non-Microsoft gateways.
microsoft.fix: For more information, see Forwarded or relayed email messages from Microsoft 365 are rejected with error 5.7.367.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Access denied, spam abuse detected
microsoft.why: The sending account was banned because of detected spam activity.
microsoft.fix: For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 451 5.7.500-699 (ASxxx) in Exchange Online. Verify that account issues are resolved, and reset the account credentials. To restore this account's ability to send mail, contact Microsoft Support through your regular channel.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Access denied, banned sender
microsoft.why: The sending account was banned because of detected spam activity.
microsoft.fix: Verify that account issues are resolved, and reset its credentials. To restore this account's ability to send mail, contact support through your regular channel.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Access denied, banned sender
microsoft.why: The sending account was banned because of detected spam activity.
microsoft.fix: Verify that account issues are resolved, and reset its credentials. To restore this account's ability to send mail, contact support through your regular channel.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: [email@contoso.com]: Recipient address rejected: Access denied
microsoft.why: The recipient address that you're trying to contact isn't valid.
microsoft.fix: Verify the recipient's email address, and try again.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Access denied, banned recipient
microsoft.why: The recipient that you're trying to contact isn't valid.
microsoft.fix: If you feel this is an error, contact support.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Access Denied, Bad HELO
microsoft.why: Your server is trying to introduce itself (HELO according to RFC 821) as the server it's trying to connect to, rather than its own fully qualified domain name.
microsoft.fix: This behavior isn't allowed, and it's characteristic of typical spambot behavior.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Access denied, rejected by recipient
microsoft.why: The recipient's organization blocked the IP from which you're trying to send.
microsoft.fix: To resolve this issue, contact the recipient.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Access denied, [$SenderIPAddress] has exceeded permitted limits within $range range
microsoft.why: The sender's IPv6 range tried to send too many messages in too short a time period.
microsoft.fix: Not applicable
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Access denied, sending domain [$SenderDomain] does not pass DMARC verification and has a DMARC policy of reject.
microsoft.why: The sender's domain in the 5322.From address doesn't pass DMARC.
microsoft.fix: For information about why this error occurred, see Why does DMARC fail?. A user also receives this bounce message because it failed DMARC, and the DMARC policy is set to reject all failures. The user should contact their email administrator for more help.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Access denied, [contoso.com] does not accept email over IPv6
microsoft.why: The sender is trying to transmit a message to the recipient over IPv6, but the recipient doesn't accept email messages over IPv6.
microsoft.fix: Not applicable
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Access denied, banned sender
microsoft.why: The IP that you're trying to send from was banned.
microsoft.fix: To delist the address, email delist@microsoft.com and provide the full NDR code and IP address. For more information, see Use the delist portal to remove yourself from the blocked senders list.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Access denied, message must be RFC 5322 section 3.6.2 compliant
microsoft.why: Message was sent without a valid "From" email address.
microsoft.fix: Office 365 only. Each message must contain a valid email address in the "From" header field. Proper formatting of this address includes angle brackets around the email address. For example: <security@contoso.com>. Without an address in this format, Microsoft 365 rejects the message.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Service unavailable, Client host [$ConnectingIP] blocked by $recipientDomain using Customer Block list (AS16012607)
microsoft.why: The recipient domain added your sending IP address to its custom block list.
microsoft.fix: The domain that received the email message blocked your sender's IP address. If you believe that your IP address was added to the recipient domain's custom block list in error, contact the recipient directly and ask them to remove it.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Access denied, Your organization does not allow external forwarding. Please contact your administrator for further assistance. AS(7555)
microsoft.why: When Exchange Online detects that a message is forwarded automatically, and an outbound spam filter policy blocks the forwarding activity, the message is restricted and this NDR is sent to the sender.
microsoft.fix: For more information, see Control automatic external email forwarding.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Access denied, banned sending IP [IP1.IP2.IP3.IP4]
microsoft.why: The IP that you're trying to send from was banned.
microsoft.fix: Verify that you're following the best practices for email deliverability, and make sure that your IP's reputations aren't degraded because of compromise or malicious traffic. If you believe that you're receiving this message in error, use the self-service portal to request that your IP address be removed from this list. For more information, see Use the delist portal to remove yourself from the blocked senders list.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Your message can't be delivered because messages to XXX, YYY are blocked by your organization using Tenant Allow Block List.
microsoft.why: Someone in your organization sent mail to an email address or domain that's blocked in the Tenant Allow/Block List. The whole message is blocked for all internal and external recipients of the message, even if only one recipient email address or domain is defined in a block entry.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Service unavailable. Client blocked from sending from unregistered domains
microsoft.why: A suspicious number of messages from unprovisioned domains is coming from this tenant.
microsoft.fix: Add and validate any or all domains that you use to send email from Microsoft 365. For more information, see Fix email delivery issues for error codes 5.7.700 through 5.7.750 in Exchange Online.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

microsoft.sample: Access denied, banned sender
microsoft.why: The EHLO, P1, or P2 sender domain of this message was banned because of detected spam activity.
microsoft.fix: To restore this domain's ability to send mail, contact Microsoft support.
microsoft.source: Microsoft Learn, Exchange Online NDR reference

4: A temporary failure. The same request may well succeed later, so the sender is expected to retry.
5: A permanent failure. Retrying the same request is not expected to work, and repeated attempts cost sender reputation.

0: The receiver said only which class of problem it hit, not what the problem was.
1: Something about the sender or recipient address.
2: The mailbox exists as an address but cannot take the message right now, or at all.
3: The receiving system itself: capacity, storage, or a message too large for it.
4: Getting to the destination, rather than anything about the destination.
5: The SMTP conversation itself went wrong.
6: The content, encoding or conversion of the message.
7: A deliberate decision by the receiver: authentication, reputation, or a rule.
